copy.blurb:
The model fancies Korea Republic more than the market does in this FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture against South Africa. +17.8pp is one of the widest in the priced field; that's what fires this as a Pick on the away side.

Elo numbers going in: South Africa 1620, Korea Republic 1790. That's a 170-point lead for Korea Republic — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: South Africa to win at 22%, the draw at 20%, and Korea Republic to win at 58%. The away side reads 58% on this distribution — the model's central case for Korea Republic.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: South Africa to win at 28%, the draw at 31%, and Korea Republic to win at 40%. On the Korea Republic side specifically the market reads 40%, which prices out at American odds of +147. Compared against the model's 58%, that's the +17.8pp gap the Pick rests on.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the Korea Republic side that lower bound is 50% — +9.4pp clear of the market's 40%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. Calibration tracks the closing market on the bulk sample; selection — picking the single side where the gap is wide — is where the engine's edge has to come from. This verdict is a selection call on the Korea Republic side.

The number above is the most recent read; it isn't frozen. With kickoff roughly 37 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. Injury news, the actual XI, and weather conditions at kickoff all feed back into the prior when they land. We republish on every refresh. The Desk surfaces edge; what to do with that surface is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Korea Republic a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +17.8pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: Korea Republic are favourites on the market at 40% — and the model thinks the market is still underrating them. Our prior reads 58%, a +17.8pp upgrade that crosses the Pick threshold comfortably.
copy.title: South Africa v Korea Republic · the model leans Korea Republic
